exposure: Trimester-specific air pollutant exposure (CO, PM10, PM2.5, SO2, O3)
Maternal oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde (MDA), protein carbonyls (PC), total antioxidant capacity (TAC))
outcome: Infant neurodevelopment (receptive language, expressive language, socio-emotional outcomes) assessed by Bayley-III
cohort: The study analyzed 87 mother-infant pairs from the OBESO perinatal cohort in Mexico City.
finding: Trimester-specific exposures to various air pollutants (CO, PM2.5, O3, SO2, PM10) were directly associated with poorer infant neurodevelopmental outcomes at one year, while maternal inflammation and oxidative stress biomarkers did not mediate these associations.
